links.outcome: Inpatient time in notes per day before vs after ambient AI scribe implementation
links.effect: Mean time in notes per day was unchanged, from 41.9 (SD 25.59) to 41.6 (SD 27.3) min (p = .77); overall ambient AI utilization was 3%.
links.quote: Mean time in notes (SD) per day was unchanged, from 41.9 (25.59) to 41.6 (27.3) min (p = .77).

links.outcome: Fit of ambient scribe to inpatient workflows and note types; utilization by note type
links.effect: Utilization was low (3% overall; 12% of H&Ps, 2% of progress notes, 6% of consult notes). Physicians requested functionality to pull forward or add onto previously generated notes.
links.quote: Future development tailored to inpatient workflows is needed to increase adoption as organizations begin to expand ambient AI in this new clinical setting.

screen.reason: Evaluates the real-world deployment and clinician utilization of ambient AI scribes in an inpatient acute care setting, but does not compare or test specific guardrails or implementation practices.
